notes: The diagram shows a pi-stop board plugged directly onto GPIO header pins (R=GPIO22, A=GPIO27, G=GPIO17, GND). The tutorial also lists the 'or 3x LEDs and resistors' option, and the parts list includes a breadboard and 4 jumper wires, so I built the external LED circuit on a breadboard instead of modelling the pi-stop.

The catalogue entry for rpi-4b lists only GPIO_HEADER as a header port. I used per-pin port names (GPIO22, GPIO27, GPIO17, GND) on pi1, as the task instructions allow. The GND pin is the one next to GPIO17 in the diagram (physical pin 14).
The tutorial gives no resistor value. I assumed 330 ohm, which is typical for LEDs on a 3.3 V GPIO pin.

The tutorial gives no breadboard hole positions. I chose them: each channel uses its own column (5, 10, 15). The wire goes in the top bank, the resistor spans the centre gap, and the LED anode shares the resistor's bottom-bank strip. All LED cathodes go to the bottom negative rail (bn), which the GND wire feeds.
Jumper wires are modelled as plain jumper-wire (4 total). Real build would likely use male-to-female wires at the Pi end, but the parts list specifies jumper-wire.
